drivingQuestion: Who is the tanna of the prohibition?

segments.he: מָכַר לוֹ בַּיִת, מָכַר לוֹ שָׂדֶה, וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״לִכְשֶׁיִּהְיוּ לִי מָעוֹת הַחְזִירֵם לִי״ – אָסוּר. ״לִכְשֶׁיִּהְיוּ לְךָ מָעוֹת אַחֲזִירֵם לָךְ״ – מוּתָּר. מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה. דְּאִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָאָמַר צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית – מוּתָּר.
segments.en: If one «sold» another «a house» or «sold him a field, and said to» the buyer: «When I have money, give» the property «back to me» in exchange for the return of the money that you paid for it, it is «prohibited,» as this transaction is essentially a loan, with the buyer enjoying the profits of the field in the interim. But if the buyer said to him of his own accord: «When you have money I will return» the property «to you,» this is «permitted.» The Gemara again asks: «Who» is the tanna who «taught» this ruling? «Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said» that it is «not in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda. As, if» it is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, doesn’t» Rabbi Yehuda «say» that «uncertain interest is permitted?»
